title: The April 2016 solar flare in four kinds of light
body:
On April 17, 2016, an active region on the sun's edge let out a mid-level flare. This is what NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory saw, in several wavelengths of extreme ultraviolet light that our eyes can't see, colored in so we can.

Footage: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center/SDO. Music added.

title: Seven minutes from space to the surface of Mars
body:
How Perseverance got from the top of Mars's atmosphere to the ground on Feb. 18, 2021: the heat shield, the parachute, and the sky crane that lowered it on ropes.

title: How El Niño moved warm water across the Pacific
body:
A 3D look at the 2015-16 El Niño. Red is water warmer than normal, blue is cooler, and the lines show currents.

title: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is shrinking and getting taller
body:
The storm has been getting smaller across for over a century, but it isn't spinning faster. It's growing taller instead.

title: The 2017 eclipse from a million miles away
body:
NASA's EPIC camera, on NOAA's DSCOVR satellite, watched the moon's shadow cross North America on Aug. 21, 2017. Look for the dark patch over the US.
